summary: Iteration 10 testing complete for enriched Student Courses page. Backend: 9/9 pytest tests PASSED covering GET /api/students/courses enriched response (description, year, semester, student_count, assignments_count, submitted_count, reviewed_count, pending_count, progress_pct), field types/ranges, progress math, _id leak, auth gate, marker-forbidden, plus regression on assignments listing. Frontend: all new data-testids render correctly for student Alice Johnson — student-dashboard, student-hero (with first name 'Alice', XP 60, Level 1, Manage Courses button), 2 course cards (CS101 10%, CS201 0%) with progress rings, course-detail panel, stat-total/submitted/pending/reviewed (10/1/1/0), course-progress bar, assignment-search, sort-select, filter-all/todo/pending/reviewed, 10 assignment cards rendered (uuid-style testids), Manage Courses dialog with 'Your Courses' + 'Available Courses' sections, course-search-input, 2 unenroll + 83 enroll buttons. Regression passed on /analytics, /badges, /leaderboard and on submit dialog. No critical issues found.

issues: Dialog lists 80+ 'Enrol' buttons (seed test courses like TC170632/TC170634) that clutter the list; consider pagination or a max-height scroll cap. Cosmetic only.
next-deadline-card not rendered for student@test.com because all assignments on CS101 show 'Deadline passed'. Expected behaviour — cannot be validated without a future-dated assignment in seed data.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_enrolled_courses (L965): student_counts_agg double-matches {course_ids: {$in: course_ids}} before and after $unwind which works but is O(users*courses). For many users this could be slow — acceptable for current scale.
StudentDashboard.js is now ~895 lines (over 700-line guideline). Consider extracting CourseCard, StatPill, ProgressRing, ManageCoursesDialog into components/.
StudentDashboard deriveAssignmentState treats status 'feedback_released' and 'no_issues' as 'reviewed' consistently with backend bucket — good alignment.

courseStats.progress is computed client-side from assignments+submissions, duplicating the backend progress_pct calculation. Consider using the backend value for a single source of truth (currently client recomputes using latest attempt heuristics — minor risk of divergence).

Course card shows 'X total / Y done' where Y comes from submitted_count; reviewed_count (feedback released) is not shown on the card — may confuse students who have reviewed work. Minor UX suggestion.
server.py remains at 3010 lines — same long-file concern as iteration 9.
